source_text: Τοὺς δὲ ἐν τῷ πεδίῳ εὑρόντας τι ἢ ἐν ταῖς ἑαυτῶν οἰκίαις, καταλειφθὲν ὑπὸ τῶν βαρβάρων, ἐὰν μὲν κατηγορηθέντες ἐλεγχθῶσιν, ὁμοίως ἐν τοῖς ὑποπίπτουσιν, ἐὰν δὲ ἑαυτοὺς ἐξείπωσι καὶ ἀποδῶσι, καὶ τῆς εὐχῆς ἀξιῶσαι.
thought_title: Penance for captives found in fields or own homes
orientation: Gregory continues his instructions to the bishop about handling captives, now addressing those found in fields or their own houses left by barbarians, setting conditions for their restoration to prayer.
pass_a_gloss: But those found in the field something or in their own houses, left by the barbarians, if indeed accused they are convicted, similarly among those who are falling under suspicion, if however they confess themselves and give satisfaction, also [they are] to be deemed worthy of the prayer.

lemmas.gloss: having found, found (participle aorist active accusative plural masculine)

choices.why: LXX Deuteronomy 22:25 uses ἐν τῷ πεδίῳ for 'in the field/open country'; matches the scriptural echo in the next section about the violated woman.
Passive participle with ὑπό expresses the agent who left these people behind; consistent with the brief's term 'barbarians' for βάρβαροι.
Middle voice of ἐξομολογέομαι means 'confess openly/fully'; reflexive 'themselves' captures the middle force in this penitential context.
Technical penitential term: 'render what is due' i.e. perform the assigned satisfaction/penance; matches the brief's 'give satisfaction'.
Aorist active infinitive of ἀξιόω; the bishop is to judge them worthy of the church's prayers (εὐχαί per glossary).

bible_refs.note: The phrase ἐν τῷ πεδίῳ echoes the LXX setting for the woman violated in the field, which Gregory invokes in the next section.

pass_b_english: But those who found something in the field or in their own houses, left there by the barbarians -- if they are accused and convicted, let them likewise be placed among the prostrators. If, however, they confess and make satisfaction, then deem them worthy of the prayers.
notes: The word τι ('something') after εὑρόντας is unusual; it may be a textual corruption for τινὰς ('some persons') or τινὰ ('someone'), but the source reads τι and it is glossed as 'something' above.

problems.quote: But those found in the field or in their own houses, left there by the barbarians
problems.source_quote: Τοὺς δὲ ἐν τῷ πεδίῳ εὑρόντας τι ἢ ἐν ταῖς ἑαυτῶν οἰκίαις, καταλειφθὲν ὑπὸ τῶν βαρβάρων
problems.why: εὑρόντας τι is active: these people found something the barbarians left behind. The English makes the people themselves the ones found and left behind, and it drops 'something'.
problems.fix: But as for those who found something in the field or in their own houses that the barbarians had left behind

problems.quote: the same as those who fall under suspicion
problems.why: οἱ ὑποπίπτοντες is the penitential grade of the 'prostrators' or kneelers. It has nothing to do with suspicion, so the English loses the penalty being assigned.
problems.fix: let them likewise be placed among the prostrators (the penitents who kneel)
problems.ruling: τοῖς ὑποπίπτουσιν is a penitential class, not 'suspicion'; English misstates whom they match.

edits.old: But those found in the field or in their own houses, left there by the barbarians
edits.new: But those who found something in the field or in their own houses, left there by the barbarians

edits.old: you must treat them the same as those who fall under suspicion
edits.new: let them likewise be placed among the prostrators

fixed: [agency] fixed: eὑρόντας τι is active and takes τι as object; English now has them finding something left behind.
[mistranslation] fixed: ὁμοίως ἐν τοῖς ὑποπίπτουσιν is the penitential grade of prostrators, not suspicion; English now assigns that penalty.
